data.narrative:
Marvel Fusion, a Series B nuclear energy company that has raised $400M+, is evaluated against a comp universe of 3 public and 8 private frontier nuclear peers including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and Fuse Energy. This sector remains highly specialized with limited same-stage comparables for direct valuation anchoring.

The analysis applies one primary method: stage-progression triangulation. Using the $400M total capital raised as a base proxy and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B advancement yields an implied valuation of $760M. This reflects the expected step-up in valuation between growth stages in venture-backed hardware. A peer-median approach was deemed inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables—while four same-sector peers exist in the broader nuclear energy landscape, fewer than three datapoints aligned on stage, valuation tier, and recency, making sector-wide aggregation unreliable and potentially misleading.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $646M (low) to $874M (high), with a median of $760M. However, this range rests on a single methodology; the reliance on stage-progression alone limits confidence. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, technical milestone achievement, and regulatory pathway clarity—factors unresolved by available market data. Additional calibration against private nuclear energy transactions or forward financing rounds would strengthen conviction on the median estimate.
